decision_type: Soft manager risk / blocked hard schedule
must_notice: Interruptions and vague expectations are observed soft signals, not proof of abuse
Two exits without denominator/cause do not establish a high turnover rate
Daily care-time constraint is hard; generic flexibility conflicts with department discretion
must_not_assume: Manager is confirmed toxic or turnover rate is known
HR typical flexibility satisfies a nonnegotiable boundary
decision_blockers: Actual 17:30 departure arrangement and late-meeting requirements
Final reporting line/scope relevant to those requirements
non_blocking_unknowns: Whether observed interruptions predict everyday relationship
acceptable_recommendations: Block signing pending a specific viable care-time arrangement; conditionally continue diligence without diagnosing manager
Decline if the hard schedule boundary is refused; soft signals can separately influence preference
unacceptable_recommendations: Accept now just because company/pay are good
Categorically label manager abusive from soft evidence
Request unrelated credentials before the schedule question
action_requirements: One focused schedule/expectations conversation or written request
Optional direct team conversation with consent, not invented reviews; avoid commitment while blocked
reconsideration_requirements: Credible written schedule plus clear goals/manager evidence may unlock conditional acceptance
evidence_requirements: Quote actual observations and mark user interpretations
Treat turnover claims as an incomplete sample, not verified statistics
boundary: No exact winner or phrase matching; no outcomes supplied. A formal contract passing does not certify semantics.
